{{Elections in Michigan}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Michigan''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect representatives for the thirteen seats in Michigan (reduced from 14 in the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|redistricting cycle]] following the [[2020 United States census]]). The deadline for candidates to file for the August 2 primary was April 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.michigan.gov/som/404|title=michigan.gov|website=www.michigan.gov}}</ref>

{{see also|Michigan's 2nd congressional district}}

The 2nd district runs along the eastern shoreline of [[Lake Michigan]] from [[Manistee, Michigan|Manistee]] to northern [[Muskegon County, Michigan|Muskegon County]], includes parts of the [[Grand Rapids, Michigan|Grand Rapids]] suburbs in [[Kent County, Michigan|Kent]] county, and parts of [[Central Michigan]], including [[Mount Pleasant, Michigan|Mount Pleasant]] and western [[Midland County, Michigan|Midland County]]. Due to redistricting, the incumbent is Republican [[John Moolenaar]] of the [[Michigan's 4th congressional district|4th congressional district]], who was re-elected with 65.0% of the vote in 2020.<ref name=":0"/>

{{see also|Michigan's 3rd congressional district}}

The 3rd district is based in [[West Michigan|western Michigan]], and includes [[Grand Rapids, Michigan|Grand Rapids]], [[Muskegon, Michigan|Muskegon]], and parts of [[Ottawa County, Michigan|Ottawa County]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Peter Meijer]], who was elected with 53.0% of the vote in 2020.<ref name=":0"/>

In the final days of the primary, the [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee]] bought $425,000 in TV ads that ostensibly attacked Gibbs (identifying him as "too conservative for West Michigan" and linking him to Trump) but were in fact designed to boost Gibbs' standing among pro-Trump Republican primary voters. The strategy—controversial within the Democratic Party—was based on the idea that Gibbs would be the weaker opponent in the general election, giving the Democrats an opportunity to win the 3rd district seat,<ref>{{cite news |last=Ax |first=Joseph |date=2022-07-26 |title=In risky midterm strategy, Democrats boost far-right candidate in Michigan race |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/risky-midterm-strategy-democrats-boost-far-right-candidate-michigan-race-2022-07-26/ |access-date=2022-07-27}}</ref><ref>Sarah Ferris and Ally Mutnick, [https://www.politico.com/news/2022/07/27/meijer-dccc-trump-primaries-00048104 House Dems berate campaign arm over 'very dangerous' GOP primary scheme], ''Politico'' (July 27, 2022).</ref><ref name=Weisman>Jonathan Weisman, [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/07/26/us/politics/democrats-john-gibbs-peter-meijer.html? Democrats Aid Far-Right Candidate Against Republican Who Backed Impeachment], ''New York Times'' (July 26, 2022).</ref> which following the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|2020 redistricting cycle]] had shifted from a Republican-leaning seat to a much more Democratic-leaning seat.<ref name=Weisman/>

The 11th district is based solely in [[Oakland County, Michigan|Oakland County]] and includes the cities of [[Royal Oak, Michigan|Royal Oak]] and [[Pontiac, Michigan|Pontiac]]. Due to redistricting, there are two incumbents in this district – Democrat [[Haley Stevens]], who was re-elected with 50.2% of the vote in 2020<ref name=":0"/> and Democrat [[Andy Levin]] of the [[Michigan's 9th congressional district|9th congressional district]], who was re-elected with 57.7% of the vote in 2020.<ref name=":0"/>

The 12th district is based in northern [[Wayne County, Michigan|Wayne County]] and includes the cities of [[Dearborn, Michigan|Dearborn]] and [[Southfield, Michigan|Southfield]]. Due to redistricting, the incumbent is Democrat [[Brenda Lawrence]] of the [[Michigan's 14th congressional district|14th congressional district]], who was re-elected with 79.3% of the vote in 2020.<ref name=":0"/> On January 4, 2022, Lawrence announced that she would not seek re-election.<ref name=Grabs/> Subsequently, Democrat [[Rashida Tlaib]] of the [[Michigan's 13th congressional district|13th congressional district]], announced she would be running in the district.<ref name=Tlaib12/> Tlaib was re-elected in 2020 with 78.1% of the vote.<ref name=":0"/>
